title: 四手联弹  (Four Hands at One Piano)

segments.t: At half past one inside sunlit Room Nine, Song slides right on the long walnut piano bench so Hao can take the lower keys on the left for their four-hand welcome duet. Listen to the whole scene first.
三点整客人就到了，宋老师，我从十二岁以后就没弹过四手联弹了！
志豪，你的左手还记得每个和弦呢，别像数砖墙一样死数拍子！
抱歉抱歉！建筑师的老毛病：一二三，到窗户正好四米整！
别老想着尺子，想想院子里那棵大树在星期五微风里轻轻摇晃的样子。
好，深吸一口气……低音大调和弦，暖暖地过渡，再轻轻拐进小调……
太好听了！听见胡桃木下排的琴弦在我高音旋律底下嗡嗡共鸣了吗？
小心——马上到第十六小节那个急转弯了，我每次到这儿就抢拍！
先听我的右手喘口气，你再接上来，就像老朋友一问一答那样自然。
一、二、接上……哎呀，中间那颗亮音就在咱俩手心之间顺顺当当唱出来了！
真棒，志豪！你的制图老教授听了，肯定笑得合不拢嘴！
等等——快看拱窗外头：小美和志鹏正端着四个热烤盘往院子里走呢！
搭档，趁浆果蛋糕在树荫下放凉，咱们从头再来一遍！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
三点整客人就到了，宋老师，我从十二岁以后就没弹过四手联弹了！

'The guest arrives at three sharp, Teacher Song, and I have not played a four-hand duet since I was twelve!' Hao marks exact clock time with "zheng" ("on the dot") after "sandian" ("three o'clock"), while "si shou lian dan" names "four-hand piano duet" by combining "four hands" and "playing together".
志豪，你的左手还记得每个和弦呢，别像数砖墙一样死数拍子！

'Your left hand still remembers every chord, Hao—stop counting beats like brick walls!' "Hexian" means "musical chord" by pairing "harmony" with "string", and "si shu" uses "si" ("rigidly" or "stubbornly") to tease stiff, mechanical counting.
抱歉抱歉！建筑师的老毛病：一二三，到窗户正好四米整！

'Sorry, sorry! Old architect habit: one, two, three, right at four meters to the window!' Doubling "baoqian" ("sorry") into "baoqian baoqian" makes the apology brisk and good-humored, while "lao maobing" affectionately means "old habit" or "pet quirk".
别老想着尺子，想想院子里那棵大树在星期五微风里轻轻摇晃的样子。

'Forget the ruler—picture the big courtyard tree swaying softly in the Friday breeze.' "Qingqing yaohuang" pairs doubled "qing" ("lightly") with "yaohuang" ("to sway") to paint a gentle rhythmic motion.
好，深吸一口气……低音大调和弦，暖暖地过渡，再轻轻拐进小调……

'All right, deep breath... low major chord, a warm shift, then a soft turn into minor...' "Shen xi yi kou qi" is the standard way to say "take a deep breath", using "kou" (literally "mouth") to count a breath of air.
太好听了！听见胡桃木下排的琴弦在我高音旋律底下嗡嗡共鸣了吗？
'Lovely! Do you hear the lower walnut strings humming richly beneath my upper melody?' "Wengweng" imitates a warm low hum, and "gongming" means "resonance"—combining "together" and "singing out".
小心——马上到第十六小节那个急转弯了，我每次到这儿就抢拍！

'Watch out—here comes that sharp turn at bar sixteen where I always rush the beat!' In music, "xiaojie" means "measure" or "bar", while "qiangpai" literally says "snatching the beat" for rushing ahead of tempo.
先听我的右手喘口气，你再接上来，就像老朋友一问一答那样自然。

'Wait for my right hand to take a breath first, then step right in as naturally as old friends trading replies.' "Chuan kou qi" literally means "catch a breath", and "yi wen yi da" ("one asks, one answers") captures easy musical back-and-forth.
一、二、接上……哎呀，中间那颗亮音就在咱俩手心之间顺顺当当唱出来了！

'One, two, step in... hey, that bright middle note sang out smoothly right between our hands!' "Zanlia" is a cozy spoken contraction for "the two of us", and "shunshundangdang" turns "smooth" into a cheerful four-syllable rhythm.
真棒，志豪！你的制图老教授听了，肯定笑得合不拢嘴！

'Bravo, Hao! Your old cartography professor is going to smile from ear to ear!' "He bu long zui" paints a grin so wide you literally "cannot close your mouth", while "kending" carries a confident "surely".
等等——快看拱窗外头：小美和志鹏正端着四个热烤盘往院子里走呢！

'Wait—look out the arched window: Mei and Peng are carrying four hot baking tins into the courtyard!' Putting "zheng" before "duanzhe" ("carrying flat in both hands") catches an action right in progress.
搭档，趁浆果蛋糕在树荫下放凉，咱们从头再来一遍！

'Partner, let us take it from the top one more time while those berry cakes cool in the shade!' "Dadang" means "partner" for a team effort, and "fangliang" joins "set aside" with "cool" to mean "let something cool down".

Deep low chords and bright treble blend smoothly through the open green shutters as four golden cakes emerge into the courtyard! See you next time.
回头见！
